title: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — civil cases in India (overview)
text: A civil case is a non-criminal legal dispute in which one party (the plaintiff) claims that another party (the defendant) has infringed a private right or failed to carry a legal obligation, and asks a civil court for a remedy such as a declaration, injunction, or damages. Typical civil matters include property and partition disputes, contract and money-recovery claims, family disputes such as divorce or succession, and tort claims. In India the procedure for deciding such disputes in civil courts is governed by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act No. 5 of 1908). The Code regulates how suits are instituted by a plaint, how defendants reply through a written statement, how issues are framed, how evidence is taken, and how decrees are executed. Civil cases are decided on the preponderance of probabilities and are distinct from criminal cases, in which the State prosecutes an alleged offence against society and the possible outcomes include fine or imprisonment.

title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
text: The Supreme Court held that arrest in offences punishable with imprisonment up to seven years must not be routine. Police must record reasons and satisfy the checklist under Section 41 CrPC. Magistrates must not authorise detention mechanically. The judgment is frequently cited in bail and arrest-procedure arguments. title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab

title: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 — Section 439
text: Section 439 CrPC confers special powers on High Courts and Courts of Session regarding bail. The court may direct that any person accused of an offence and in custody be released on bail, and may impose conditions in the interest of justice. title: Constitution of India — Article 21
text: Article 21 provides that no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Indian courts have interpreted this guarantee in a line of public authorities, including Maneka Gandhi. This excerpt is statutory legal-authority context from India Code, not a case-file exhibit.

title: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 — Section 438
text: Section 438 CrPC deals with direction for grant of bail to a person apprehending arrest. The High Court or Court of Session may, if it thinks fit, direct that in the event of arrest the person shall be released on bail. Conditions may be imposed.
